**Verdict: PASS for DG0 round 27, with no findings of any severity.** All 12 checks ran and passed on the frozen candidate `sha256:9420948b…8128` (commit `49b5ad7`), and the pre-freeze script exited 0 with all 11 of its checks passing. **Candidate check.** HEAD is `a4c6f82`, not `49b5ad7`. That commit only adds the round's assignments, the candidate manifest and `stages.json`, all of which are outside the candidate. The candidate ID recomputes the same in the main repo and in a fresh full (`--no-local`) clone at `49b5ad7`. The only change since round 26 is comment text in `rules.mjs` plus the D-043 entry in `decisions.md`; no executable line changed. **What I checked:** 1. **Extraction.** I pulled the text straight out of the docx: 1001 paragraphs and table cells across 49 tables. None are missing from `playbook.md`. The 15 that don't match word for word are split by line breaks in the docx and appear with `
` in the markdown. The shipped extraction check also passes. 2. **Coverage.** All 165 playbook blocks have a disposition. No block is left without a requirement and no mapping points at a missing one. Re-running the merge script reproduces the register and the coverage file byte for byte. 3. **Templates.** Every T01–T16 column appears verbatim in both the field inventory and the register. So do all the value lists, the 25/25/20/15/15 weights, the waves, the T10 RAG rules, the T11 approvers and SLAs, and the T12 RACI. 4. **Deliverables.** All of these are present: the 14 charter fields, the 5 scope checks, the 10 TOM dimensions and canvas prompts, the 25 health-check questions with their score and top-3 actions, G1–G6, the minimum roles, and the roaming example. Principles written as prose are covered by the requirements they map to; I read each of those rows. 5. **No invented source requirements.** Every SOURCE row cites a playbook block, and every USER or ENGINEERING row cites the master prompt. 6. **Provenance.** Nothing claims official PMI status, certification or Mobily branding. `#0078FF` appears only as a colour that must not be used for buttons. 7. **Operating logic.** Each rule has a testable acceptance criterion: - RAG comes from the trajectory, not task completion; - an initiative can't close without validated benefits; - value still awaiting Finance validation is kept out of validated totals; - a shared benefit counts once; - allocation over 100% is rejected, and anything under 100% shows as unallocated; - technical admins can't approve; - G6 never implies DG7. 8. **Master-prompt sample.** Every 7th block (61 blocks, §0–§21, including table rows) has a sensible disposition and mapping. 9. **Staging.** Every requirement's final gate matches its last increment and follows §21. The two exceptions have reasons given in the stage plan: REQ-PB-032 needs the P3 initiatives, and REQ-PB-093 is a P5 Studio setting. 10. **Glossary, journeys, permissions.** The Arabic terms are sensible and marked for review by a Mobily language owner. The journeys cover all six phases and gates plus modular entry, KPI updates, Finance validation, committees, BAU handover and admin publishing. The permissions matrix follows the playbook roles, T11 and the RACI. **The D-043 change and D-039.** The `commitPresent()` comment now states no closure policy. The `checkClosure` comment matches the code: the frozen-round check always applies. D-039's clean-up claim holds, because only round 18's commit (`450c756f`) is absent, in both the clone and the main repo. D-043's "57" is the validator test count; the full gate suite passes 63 of 63. Neither entry says anything about business rules or provenance. Two things I noted but didn't raise as findings: - **Round number.** `review-common.md` says "Review round: 23", but the paths and task ID say 27. I recorded round 27. - **One comment's wording.** The `isShallow` comment in `rules.mjs` says "tolerances" (plural), while elsewhere there's a single one. It describes clone depth, not closures, so it's code-security's call. My earlier findings F-DG0-013 and F-DG0-014 were already closed as verified, so there was nothing for me to re-verify. I've written the record, which passes the schema check and whose evidence paths all exist, plus a short narrative and the evidence logs. The disposable clones are deleted. Files are in `docs/delivery/`: - `reviews/DG0/round-27/domain-reviewer.json` - `reviews/DG0/round-27/domain-reviewer.md` - `test-evidence/DG0/domain/round-27/`
